name: Question 10
problem:
Which of the following integrals evaluates to zero due to symmetry?

- ${\int }_{-1/2}^{1/2}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x$
- ${\int }_{-\pi /8}^{\pi /8}\frac{{x}^{4}+2}{3}\,\text{d}x$
- ${\int }_{-3}^{3}({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x})\,\text{d}x$
worked_solution:
Recall the following:

- a function $f(x)$ is *even* if $f(-x)=f(x)$

- a function $f(x)$ is *odd* if $f(-x)=-f(x)$

Moreover, for any odd function $f(x),$ the graph of $y=f(x)$ has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin, so we have

$$
{\int }_{-a}^{a}f(x)\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

So, to determine which integrals evaluate to $0$ due to symmetry, we have to determine which integrands are odd functions.

- The function $f(x)={x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ is an odd function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-x) & =(-x)^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-x) \\  & ={x}^{2}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\  & =-f(x)\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by symmetry, we can conclude that

$$
{\int }_{-1/2}^{1/2}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

- The function $g(x)=\frac{{x}^{4}+2}{3}$ is *not* an odd function:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(-x) & =\frac{(-x)^{4}+2}{3} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{4}+2}{3} \\  & \ne -g(x)\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- The function $h(x)={e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}$ is an odd function:

$$
\begin{aligned}h(-x) & ={e}^{-x}-{e}^{-(-x)} \\  & ={e}^{-x}-{e}^{x} \\  & =-({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}) \\  & =-h(x)\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by symmetry, we can conclude that

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{3}({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x})\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
